title: Things To Do in Segovia in 48 Hours

items.name: Segovia Cathedral
items.details: Start at the last Gothic cathedral built in Spain; Flemish tapestries, marble statues

items.name: La Almuzara
items.details: Artsy vegan-friendly cafe next to the Cathedral; she recommends guacamole with chips and the grapefruit and avocado salad. Alternative for cochinillo: Meson de Candido

items.name: Alcazar of Segovia
items.details: World Heritage Site, supposed inspiration for Disney's Cinderella Castle; Hall of Kings frieze; viewpoint walk to Mirador de la Pradera de San Marcos

items.name: Church of Vera Cruz
items.details: Consecrated 1208, built by the Knights Templar; secluded Romanesque church

items.name: Casa de la Moneda Museum
items.details: Museo Casa de la Moneda - history of money and the Spanish Royal Mint's machinery; nearby Jardines Del Rey for a short walk

items.name: Parador de Segovia
items.details: Dinner on the hotel terrace with sunset views over the city; full meal or a glass of local red wine. She provides a 2km walking map for the day

items.name: La Granja de San Ildefonso
items.details: Day 2: hire a car or taxi. Philip V's Versailles-modelled palace in the hills; remarkable interiors, 26 fountains incl. the Baths of Diana; gardens free to walk

items.name: La Huerta De San Lorenzo
items.details: Hidden-gem restaurant: sustainably produced vegetables farmed on site, organic wine; overnight rooms upstairs

items.name: Aqueduct of Segovia
items.details: 2000-year-old Roman aqueduct, mortar-free stones, in use until mid-19th century; Loba Capitolina sculpture in front

items.name: Jewish Quarter (La Juderia)
items.details: One of Castile's richest former Jewish quarters; Corpus Christi Convent (former Main Synagogue)

items.name: El Fogon Sefardi
items.details: Traditional Sephardic dishes with local Castilian influence in the Jewish Quarter; alternative: touristy creperie on Plaza del Azoguejo with aqueduct views

items.name: Madrid train
items.details: Fly to Madrid then 30-minute train to Segovia; she recommends a full weekend over a day trip

items.name: Mahon
items.details: Menorca's capital; Sant Jaume Festival July 24-26 (live music, fireworks, horses); try Xoriguer gin and pomada; her favorite drink spot was Bar Lemon

items.name: Mahon Harbour + Isla del Lazareto
items.details: Explore by boat; she liked the glass-bottomed boats from Yellow Catamarans; boat to Isla del Lazareto (19th-century quarantine island) with sunset views over the harbour

items.name: Playa de Cavalleria
items.details: Natural beach on the north coast, ~10-min walk from free car park; no shops - bring water and snacks

items.name: Binidali
items.details: Small quiet beach with aquamarine water and a beach bar above; nearby Cala Biniparratx for limestone gorge and sheltered cove

items.name: Ciutadella
items.details: Her favorite town on the island; romantic side streets and port; try an ensaimada pastry; boutique hotels

items.name: Binibeca
items.details: 1972 architect-designed 'fishermen's village' - white facades, cobbled streets, authentic look

items.name: El Toro
items.details: Menorca's tallest hill (342m) with island-wide views; Sanctuary of the Verge del Toro and Christ statue on top

items.name: S'Algar / Cala Alcaufar
items.details: Purpose-built resort but peaceful Cala Alcaufar beach with one bar/restaurant; rock formations; good for sunset

items.name: Binifadet Winery
items.details: Free guided winery tour, vineyards, wine on the porch; unpretentious local cuisine (sobrasada, fish marinated in Xoriguer gin)

items.name: Cova d'en Xoroi
items.details: Cave bar perched above the sea - her pick for a sundowner

items.name: Toroko National Park
items.details: Recommended by Nataly 'for the ultimate escape into an untouched environment that stands in complete contrast to buzzing Taipei'; article spells it 'Toroko', commonly Taroko

items.name: Fo Guang temple
items.details: Described as one of their favourite temples, decorated by a huge statue of Buddha at its entrance

items.name: Alishan region
items.details: Murad: 'we were quickly enchanted by the mountains and forests of the Alishan region, which truly looks like some sort of fairy-tale'

items.name: Emerald tea plantations and tea houses
items.details: Murad advises paying a visit to the emerald tea plantations 'which I'm sure would rival even the finest of those in India and Sri Lanka'; tea houses host traditional tea ceremonies; they especially liked the ulun variety, fragrant and subtle with a slightly spicy taste

title: Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek - Ultimate Guide and Itinerary

items.name: Marigold Hotel (Amrit Tours)
items.details: Mark booked everything through Marigold Hotel/Amrit Tours in Pokhara; arranged permits and a guide ($20/day, 5 days = $100). Rooms around 700 Rupees.

items.name: Taxi from Pokhara to Nayapul
items.details: Started at about 8 am; taxi cost 1,500 Nepali Rupees. Trekking time about 5-6 hours.

items.name: Green Land Restaurant
items.details: Small house restaurant lunch stop; vegetarian dal bhat for 300 Rupees, all the rice he could eat.

items.name: Tikhedunga Guest House
items.details: Double room 350 Rupees; dinner of plain rice (150), stir fried veg noodles (270), tea (50).

items.name: Hike Tikhedunga to Ghorepani
items.details: Walked straight up the mountain ~4 hours, glimpses of snow-capped Annapurna peaks; lunch of sukuti (dry buffalo) fried with onions and spices for 400 Rupees; total hiking 7-8 hours.

items.name: Dhaulagiri Lodge
items.details: Top of the village in the main square area; 300 Rupees room, 100 Rupees hot shower; dinner of vegetable fried rice (260) and milk tea (60).

items.name: Sunrise at Poon Hill summit
items.details: 5 am climb (45 minutes) to 3,210m summit for sunrise over the Annapurna range; then hiked the parallel ridge down to Gandruk; lunch of vegetarian dal bhat for 360 Rupees; total hiking 10-12 hours.

items.name: Muna Hotel
items.details: 350 Rupees per night.

items.name: Hike Gandruk to Deurali
items.details: Mostly downhill stone steps through small villages and farms; breakfast of dal baht (360 Rupees); total hiking about 10 hours.

items.name: Hotel Trekkers Inn
items.details: Room 350 Rupees; dinner of Tibet bread (140) and omelet with rice (320).

items.name: Hike Deurali to Pothana, taxi to Pokhara
items.details: About an hour to the permit check town of Pothana, then onward to the Annapurna Eco Village (1,000 Rupees/night, stayed 1 night) before catching a taxi back to Pokhara.

title: The Ultimate Guide to Riding the Trans-Siberian Railway (Moscow to Vladivostok)
destination: Moscow to Vladivostok, via Irkutsk and Ulan-Ude

items.name: Trans-Siberian train: Moscow to Irkutsk
items.details: 74 hours of non-stop train travel; first leg of the journey. Source also covers visa process, ticket buying, and train-class choices.

items.name: Irkutsk - Lake Baikal (Olkhon Island)
items.details: Stopped in Irkutsk for two nights. Main draw is Lake Baikal, the deepest lake in the world; Olkhon Island is the popular overnight island (ferry), but needs at least 3 days total (7h travel each leg), which they wish they'd scheduled.

items.name: Train: Irkutsk to Ulan-Ude
items.details: Short 6.5 hour ride to the second stop, Ulan-Ude.

items.name: Ulan-Ude sightseeing
items.details: Stayed two nights, but they say one day is enough: world's largest statue of Lenin's head, main walking street, a church near the end of the walking street, a monastery on a hill overlooking the city, and another monastery 45 minutes outside the city.

items.name: Train: Ulan-Ude to Vladivostok
items.details: Final leg: another 64 hours of non-stop train travel to Vladivostok. They found no interesting stops between Ulan-Ude and Vladivostok.

items.name: Vladivostok stopover
items.details: End of the railway journey; they note their Vladivostok time was cut short by their onward flight needs and would have spent more time there.

items.name: Russian visa logistics (pre-trip)
items.details: Three-step visa process for US passport holders: letter of invitation (they got one via Fortuna Travel for $12 after VisaHQ quoted $50/person for the letter), visa application (delivered in person to a Russian consulate or via visa service), and visa registration within 7 working days in Russia.

items.name: Suggested additional stops: Kazan and Yekaterinburg
items.details: Locals in Moscow recommended stopping in Kazan (predominantly Muslim city); they also recommend booking a stop in Yekaterinburg (where the last tsar was executed) for those interested in Russian history.

title: Visit Borneo: Derawan Islands guide by Emmett Sparling

items.name: Boat from Tarakan
items.details: 5-hour boat ride from Tarakan to reach Derawan Islands, per Sparling's guide

items.name: Derawan Island homestay
items.details: About six homestays on Derawan Island, all huts on stilts over the water

items.name: Warungs
items.details: Basic restaurants called Warungs - like an Indonesian Subway; traditional Indonesian food for lunch and dinner

items.name: Jellyfish Lake
items.details: 2-4 hour speed boat ride from Derawan; swim among millions of harmless jellyfish

items.name: Snorkelling / free diving
items.details: Beautiful snorkelling/free-diving spots from Jellyfish Lake to the underwater forest

items.name: Bike around Derawan
items.details: Rent bikes and ride around Derawan Island in about 30 minutes, stopping at local spots

items.name: Light-beam canyon
items.details: Canyon where light beams shine through at certain times of day; ask a local how to reach it

items.name: Arrival and hotel transfer
items.details: Arrival in Kathmandu (1300m) and transfer to hotel.

items.name: Travel to Pokhara
items.details: Fly or drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara (823m); 7-8 hours by road.

items.name: Trek Pokhara to Kalikasthan
items.details: Trek from Pokhara to Kalikasthan (1,370m). Full board camping accommodation with three meals a day during the trek; camping crew and logistical support.

items.name: Trek to Syaklung
items.details: Trek route: Kalikasthan - Thulokot - Mathi Thana - Naudanda to Syaklung (1,730m).

items.name: Trek to Chisapani Danda
items.details: Trek from Syaklung to Chisapani Danda (1550m).

items.name: Trek to Begnas Tal, return to Pokhara
items.details: Trek from Chisapani to Begnas Tal, then drive back to Pokhara.

items.name: Return to Kathmandu
items.details: Drive from Pokhara back to Kathmandu, 7-8 hours. Farewell dinner included in package.

items.name: Package inclusions
items.details: Package includes: airport pickup/drop-off, 3-star hotel in Kathmandu on B/B plan, land transport, TIMS permit, equipped/insured trekking porter (1 per 2 persons, carries 25kg), experienced first-aid-trained English-speaking guide, full-board camping with three meals daily, camping crew. Grade: easy. Best season: spring/autumn.
